stem: An older adult in the ICU has multiple modifiable delirium risks, including disrupted sleep, immobility, and impaired hearing. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Keep the room dark and avoid orientation or conversation throughout the day
options.B: Use continuous television and frequent overnight waking to increase stimulation
options.C: Remove clocks, hearing aids, eyeglasses, and family orientation cues
options.D: Use a multicomponent nonpharmacologic plan that supports orientation/cognition, sleep, mobility, and hearing or vision needs

rationale: SCCM's current PADIS guideline listing retains the recommendation for a multicomponent, nonpharmacologic delirium intervention aimed at modifiable risks and at improving cognition, sleep, mobility, hearing, and vision. Examples include reorientation, reducing nighttime light/noise, mobilization/rehabilitation as appropriate, and use of hearing aids or eyeglasses. The 2025 focused update also supports enhanced ICU mobilization/rehabilitation. D is correct.
educational_objective: Select a multicomponent nonpharmacologic strategy to reduce modifiable ICU delirium risk factors.

blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — ICU delirium prevention

source_original.stem: An older adult in the ICU is at risk for delirium and has limited mobility, disrupted sleep, and impaired hearing. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Keep the room dark and minimize all conversation throughout the day so the client receives as little stimulation as possible between nursing procedures.
options.B: Use continuous television and frequent waking overnight to provide stimulation, even when the client is sleeping or does not want additional activity.
options.C: Avoid clocks, calendars, hearing aids, and family interaction because orientation cues can increase confusion in clients who are critically ill.
options.D: Use a multicomponent delirium-prevention approach with reorientation, sleep support, mobility as appropriate, and access to hearing or vision aids.

source_original.rationale: ICU delirium prevention is multicomponent rather than based on either sensory deprivation or indiscriminate stimulation. Measures include regular reorientation, sleep promotion, early mobility when appropriate, and correction of sensory impairment with hearing or vision aids.
source_original.source_detail: SCCM PADIS nonpharmacologic delirium recommendation: multicomponent intervention targeting cognition, sleep, mobility, hearing and vision, including reorientation and sensory aids. 2018 PADIS with 2025 focused update/current SCCM listing; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Verified that SCCM still lists the 2018 multicomponent nonpharmacologic delirium recommendation alongside its 2025 focused update and added the 2025 mobilization support. Simplified distractors, reduced difficulty from hard to medium, and corrected blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests prevention of a critical-care complication.

audit_findings.source_authority: SCCM PADIS current listing and 2025 focused update; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: SCCM current guideline pages checked 2026-08-17; 2025 focused update explicitly links the 2018 guideline as related/current core guidance.
audit_findings.claim_audit: SCCM directly supports a multicomponent nonpharmacologic intervention targeting cognition, sleep, mobility, hearing, and vision; 2025 update supports enhanced mobilization.

distractor_audit.A: Sensory deprivation and lack of orientation are contrary to the multicomponent recommendation.
distractor_audit.B: Sleep disruption is a modifiable risk, not a prevention strategy.
distractor_audit.C: Hearing/vision aids and orientation cues are components of the recommended intervention.

audit_findings.cueing: Shortened all alternatives to comparable intervention statements.
audit_findings.blueprint: Prevention of ICU delirium as a potential complication fits Reduction of Risk Potential.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked SCCM 2018 current listing and 2025 update; D/category 9 remain correct.
